--- title: "07 — fgsea: what's enriched among vent-associated KOs" subtitle: "Frenemies euk metaT — grain 4, vent vs. non-vent contrast, ranked by Cliff's delta on rCLR" author: "Hu Lab" date: last-modified format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 2 code-fold: show df-print: paged --- # Set up One ranked list, one fgsea call. The span classes from 06 (class-, phylum-, supergroup-restricted, cross-supergroup; 2026-10-12, replacing the earlier taxon-count breadth classes) are tested as gene sets alongside the heterotrophy subcategories and KEGG pathways — they are not used to split the analysis into separate runs (2026-09-25 decision). >SKH: updated 2026-10-12 for the 06 rebuild (span classes, carrier control). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # locator: root (render) or scripts/ (interactive) source(if (file.exists("_setup.R")) "_setup.R" else "scripts/_setup.R") ``` ::: ## Assign parameters Same vent scope and grain as 04/06, so the ranked list and the span classes describe the same feature space. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} FIELDS_IN_SCOPE <- c("Gorda Ridge", "Von Damm", "Piccard") CHOSEN_DEPTH <- 4 # grain locked in 02 MIN_SET_SIZE <- 5 # gene sets below this are dropped before fgsea # (deliberately low: het-category/KEGG-pathway membership # is partial — see "Gene sets" below — not the usual 15) SPAN_TABLE <- "output-tables/06_ko_span.csv" # from 06 (universe + span classes) # Heterotrophy / phagotrophy KO panel, compiled once by # scripts/00_build_het_gene_reference.R. 06 reads the same file, so the gene sets # below and 06's span classes describe the same panel by construction. HET_REFERENCE <- "data/gene-lists/het_gene_reference.csv" # >SKH: KEGG level-C pathways (four Cellular/Environmental categories) and the Burns et al. # 2018 trophic-mode families, compiled by scripts/00b_build_trophic_gene_sets.R (2026-10-22) TROPHIC_SETS <- "data/gene-lists/trophic_gene_sets.csv" ``` ::: # Ranked list: vent vs. non-vent contrast for each vent-associated KO Ranking statistic = **Cliff's delta between vent and non-vent sample units** for each KO's robust-CLR values (`contrast_ranks()`, `R/cliffs_delta.R`). Positive delta means that KO ranks higher at vents; the magnitude is the net share of vent/non-vent unit pairs agreeing on the direction (Cliff 1993, Psychol Bull 114:494-509; Vargha and Delaney 2000, J Educ Behav Stat 25:101-132). **This reverses the note that a vent-vs-non-vent contrast must not enter through fgsea** (that note dated 2026-09-25; reversed 2026-09-27). The reason the differential was dropped is specific to the *KO-level* test: with 13 vent and 6 non-vent units, no permutation p reaches BH significance and the differential set empties. fgsea never tests a KO on its own, it asks whether a whole gene set sits toward one end of the ranked list, which is the case GSEA was built for (Subramanian et al. 2005, PNAS 102:15545-15550). The set-level result is a different test at a different resolution, not a re-entry of the dropped one, and it does not depend on any single KO clearing max-T. Keep saying *relative*: this is compositional. The universe is the vent-associated KO set (detected in >= 30% of vent units, i.e. >= 4 of 13, under the shared detection rule; 05), read from 06's span table rather than recomputed, so the ranked list and the gene sets below describe exactly the same KOs. Units on **both** sides of the contrast come from the full paired table (vent + non-vent), since a vent-only matrix cannot express the contrast. >SKH: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # built once at the end of 02 (R/load_paired.R) paired_all <- load_paired(fields = FIELDS_IN_SCOPE, depth = CHOSEN_DEPTH) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` [load_paired] data/processed/paired_L4.RData (built 2026-10-23 09:06; 318,911 rows) ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ko_habitat <- build_matrix(paired_all, "ko_id", min_tpm = 0, transform = params$transform, id_col = "sample_id", aggregate = "mean", unit_col = "sample_unit") # $z is the transformed matrix $dist was built from; $mat is RAW abundance. # (build_matrix() gained $z on 2026-09-27, after a ranking built here from $mat # turned out to be raw mean scaledTPM mislabelled as mean CLR.) ko_habitat_z <- ko_habitat$z habitat_by_unit <- paired_all |> distinct(sample_unit, vent_bin) |> deframe() unit_is_vent <- habitat_by_unit[rownames(ko_habitat_z)] == "Vent" stopifnot(setequal(rownames(ko_habitat_z), names(habitat_by_unit)), any(unit_is_vent), !all(unit_is_vent)) message(glue("{sum(unit_is_vent)} vent units vs {sum(!unit_is_vent)} non-vent units | ", "{ncol(ko_habitat_z)} KOs in the paired matrix")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` 13 vent units vs 6 non-vent units | 7643 KOs in the paired matrix ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ko_habitat_delta <- tibble( ko_id = colnames(ko_habitat_z), delta_vent = contrast_ranks(ko_habitat_z, habitat_by_unit, focal = "Vent") ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ko_span <- read_csv(SPAN_TABLE, show_col_types = FALSE) ranks_df <- ko_habitat_delta |> inner_join(ko_span |> select(ko_id, span_rank, top_carrier_L4), by = "ko_id") |> filter(is.finite(delta_vent)) |> arrange(desc(delta_vent)) message(glue("{nrow(ranks_df)} vent-associated KOs ranked ", "({n_distinct(ko_span$ko_id) - nrow(ranks_df)} dropped: absent from ", "the paired matrix, or non-finite delta)")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` 853 vent-associated KOs ranked (0 dropped: absent from the paired matrix, or non-finite delta) ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ranks <- ranks_df |> select(ko_id, delta_vent) |> deframe() ``` ::: ## Sign check A positive delta has to mean higher at vents. Check it against the CLR means of the two extreme KOs rather than trusting the convention, since an inverted sign would flip every NES in the table with no other symptom. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sign_check <- ranks_df |> slice(c(1, n())) |> mutate(mean_clr_vent = map_dbl(ko_id, \(k) mean(ko_habitat_z[unit_is_vent, k])), mean_clr_nonvent = map_dbl(ko_id, \(k) mean(ko_habitat_z[!unit_is_vent, k])), agrees = sign(delta_vent) == sign(mean_clr_vent - mean_clr_nonvent)) sign_check ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} stopifnot(all(sign_check$agrees)) ``` ::: # Gene sets Three sources, combined into one list and tagged so the results can be filtered or read separately. Membership from the two curated gene lists is partial — Sarah is still assigning KOs to categories/pathways — so sets are kept down to `MIN_SET_SIZE = 5` rather than the usual 15, and this should be re-run as that membership grows. ## Span classes (06) The 05 habitat classes (vent-only, vent-skewed, shared) are **not** tested here: they are defined by non-vent occupancy, so their position on a vent-vs-non-vent ranking is built in. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} span_sets <- ranks_df |> filter(span_rank != "no_carrier") |> (\(d) split(d$ko_id, d$span_rank))() |> (\(x) x[lengths(x) > 0])() tibble(pathway = names(span_sets), n = lengths(span_sets)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## Heterotrophy categories and subcategories Read from `data/gene-lists/het_gene_reference.csv`, the panel compiled by `scripts/00_build_het_gene_reference.R`. That script — not this document — resolves the awkward KEGG fields in the source lists (`"K04624-K08424 (family range)"`, `"K21348 (representative)"`, `"Not in KEGG KO (non-orthologous)"`, `;`-separated lists) and logs every unresolvable row to `output-tables/00_het_gene_reference_unresolved.csv`. **On the family-range rows** (`"K04624-K08424 (family range)"`): the builder keeps both boundary ids as members and does not expand the range. KEGG ortholog numbers are assigned roughly sequentially rather than by family, so `K04624`–`K08424` spans ~3,800 unrelated orthologs; expanding it would inject thousands of KOs with nothing to do with this gene set. Real family membership needs an actual KEGG lookup (the `ko` entry in the KEGG API), and the unresolved log records the range so that can be done deliberately. Category and pathway assignment in the curated lists is still partial, so sets are kept down to `MIN_SET_SIZE = 5` rather than the usual 15. Re-run `scripts/00_build_het_gene_reference.R` and then this document as that membership grows. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} het_ref <- read_csv(HET_REFERENCE, show_col_types = FALSE) message(glue("{n_distinct(het_ref$ko_id)} heterotrophy KOs in the panel | ", "{n_distinct(het_ref$category)} categories, ", "{n_distinct(het_ref$subcategory)} subcategories")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` 169 heterotrophy KOs in the panel | 3 categories, 25 subcategories ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Subcategory only. `category` is the parent of `subcategory` in the same # classification, so testing both put the same evidence into one BH family twice # (dropped 2026-09-27). Sets come from the long table, so a KO assigned to two # subcategories joins both. het_subcategory_sets <- het_ref |> filter(!is.na(subcategory)) |> distinct(subcategory, ko_id) |> (\(d) split(d$ko_id, d$subcategory))() |> (\(x) x[lengths(x) > 0])() tibble(pathway = names(het_subcategory_sets), n = lengths(het_subcategory_sets), source = "het_subcategory") |> arrange(desc(n)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## KEGG pathways Also from the same reference file. Only `phagotrophy_genes_protists_1.csv` carries a pathway column, and it is free text (e.g. `"ko04145 Phagosome; ko04010 MAPK signaling"`, and in at least one row the id trails the name: `"Nitrogen metabolism ko00910"`), so the builder splits it, pulls the `ko#####` id out wherever it sits, and assigns one canonical `pathway_label` per id — a single id written two different ways (`ko04142 Lysosome` and `ko04142 Lysosome (saposin-like family)`) would otherwise become two gene sets for one pathway. Sets key on `pathway_label`. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} kegg_sets <- het_ref |> filter(!is.na(pathway_label)) |> distinct(pathway_label, ko_id) |> (\(d) split(d$ko_id, d$pathway_label))() |> (\(x) x[lengths(x) > 0])() tibble(pathway = names(kegg_sets), n = lengths(kegg_sets)) |> arrange(desc(n)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## KEGG level-C pathways and Burns et al. 2018 trophic-mode families Two outside sources, so the result does not depend on hand-picked membership (2026-10-21: approaches A and B). * `kegg_level_c`: every KEGG pathway map in Transport and catabolism, Signal transduction, Cell growth and death and Cell motility, with full KEGG membership. Prokaryote-only maps (two-component system, bacterial chemotaxis, bacterial flagellar assembly, Caulobacter cell cycle) are dropped in 00b. Many signaling maps share the same kinase core, so these sets overlap; read them as one family, not as independent results. * `burns2018`: protein families whose presence predicts phagocytosis, photosynthesis or prototrophy across 35 eukaryotic genomes (Burns et al. 2018, *Nat Ecol Evol* 2:697–704), mapped from UniProt representatives to KOs in 00b. Those families were chosen to predict *gene content*; here they are tested for a *shift in expression* between habitats, which is a different question from the one they were built for. The protist experimental set (00b) is too small to clear `MIN_SET_SIZE` in this universe; 06b reports it KO by KO instead. >SKH: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} trophic_ref <- read_csv(TROPHIC_SETS, show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(set_source %in% c("kegg_level_c", "burns2018")) trophic_sets_by_source <- trophic_ref |> distinct(set_source, set_name, ko_id) |> (\(d) split(d, d$set_source))() |> map(\(d) split(d$ko_id, d$set_name)) kegg_level_c_sets <- trophic_sets_by_source$kegg_level_c %||% list() burns_sets <- trophic_sets_by_source$burns2018 %||% list() if (!length(burns_sets)) { message("No burns2018 sets in ", TROPHIC_SETS, ": run scripts/00b_build_trophic_gene_sets.R ", "once with a network connection to build the UniProt -> KO cache.") } tibble(pathway = c(names(kegg_level_c_sets), names(burns_sets)), source = rep(c("kegg_level_c", "burns2018"), c(length(kegg_level_c_sets), length(burns_sets))), n = c(lengths(kegg_level_c_sets), lengths(burns_sets)), n_ranked = map_int(c(kegg_level_c_sets, burns_sets), \(k) sum(k %in% names(ranks)))) |> arrange(source, desc(n_ranked)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## Combine, tag by source Size filtering happens on membership **inside the ranked universe**, not on raw membership. `fgsea()`'s own `minSize` applies to each set after intersecting it with `stats`, so a set with >= `MIN_SET_SIZE` KOs overall but fewer than that among the ranked KOs used to clear the filter here and then get dropped silently by `fgsea()`, which is what broke `nrow(enrich) == length(all_sets)` in the QC block (diagnosed and fixed 2026-09-27). Only the 06 class sets were ever immune, being built from `ranks_df` itself; the het and KEGG sets come from `het_gene_reference.csv`, which is not restricted to vent-associated KOs. **Multiple testing by family** (>SKH: 2026-10-22). BH is applied within each family, not across every set: the original ten (span classes + curated heterotrophy subcategories + curated KEGG pathways) stay one family, as decided 2026-10-10, so adding the outside sources does not change their adjusted p-values. `kegg_level_c` and `burns2018` are one family each. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} all_sets <- c(span_sets, het_subcategory_sets, kegg_sets, kegg_level_c_sets, burns_sets) set_source <- rep(c("span_rank", "het_subcategory", "kegg_pathway", "kegg_level_c", "burns2018"), c(length(span_sets), length(het_subcategory_sets), length(kegg_sets), length(kegg_level_c_sets), length(burns_sets))) names(set_source) <- names(all_sets) # >SKH: BH family per source (see above) set_family <- c(span_rank = "curated_panel", het_subcategory = "curated_panel", kegg_pathway = "curated_panel", kegg_level_c = "kegg_level_c", burns2018 = "burns2018") # de-duplicate names across sources before filtering by size (fgsea keys on name) names(all_sets) <- make.unique(names(all_sets)) names(set_source) <- names(all_sets) size_in_universe <- lengths(map(all_sets, intersect, names(ranks))) n_dropped <- sum(size_in_universe < MIN_SET_SIZE) all_sets <- all_sets[size_in_universe >= MIN_SET_SIZE] set_source <- set_source[names(all_sets)] message(glue("{length(all_sets)} gene sets kept | {n_dropped} dropped: fewer than ", "{MIN_SET_SIZE} members among the {length(ranks)} ranked KOs")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` 54 gene sets kept | 58 dropped: fewer than 5 members among the 853 ranked KOs ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} tibble(source = set_source) |> count(source, name = "n_sets_kept") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: # fgsea Set-level enrichment (GSEA), not a per-KO differential expression test. `fgsea()` takes the gene sets (`all_sets`) and the ranked statistic (`ranks`, Cliff's delta vent vs. non-vent) and asks whether each set sits toward one end of the ranked list. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # BiocManager::install("fgsea") library(fgsea) set.seed(params$seed) # ?fgsea() enrich <- fgsea(pathways = all_sets, stats = ranks, minSize = MIN_SET_SIZE, eps = 0) |> as_tibble() |> mutate(source = set_source[pathway], family = unname(set_family[source])) |> relocate(source, family, .after = pathway) |> # >SKH: fgsea's padj is BH across every set passed in; recompute it within family mutate(padj = p.adjust(pval, method = "BH"), .by = family) |> # A 5-KO set gives an unstable NES and a 2-3 gene leading edge. Flagged rather # than dropped, so set size travels with every claim (2026-09-27). mutate(small_set = size < 10) |> arrange(padj) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning in prepareStats(stats, scoreType, gseaParam): There are ties in the preranked stats (58.26% of the list). The order of those tied genes will be arbitrary, which may produce unexpected results. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} enrich |> select(pathway, source, family, size, small_set, NES, pval, padj) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: * Pathway: tested gene set we looked at * source: where did gene set come from. * size: number of KOs in the gene set after filtering the ranked list * NES: normalized enrichment score. neg vs. pos is the direction of the enrichment (i.e., when positive it means they are positively enriched) and the magnitude is the strenth relative to the gene-set size * pval: permutation p-value * padj: BH-adjusted p-value With the vent-vs-non-vent ranking, a positive NES means the set sits toward the vent-skewed (high-delta) end of the ranked list; negative means the non-vent-skewed end. *source*: _span_rank_ means the four 06 span classes (class-, phylum-, supergroup-restricted, cross-supergroup): is the vent-skewed signal carried by narrow or widely shared KOs? _Het_subcategory_ means that is includes the kegg pathways or het subcategory from curated gene list. This helps us understand which functional module is represented in the set looked at. _small_set_ flags sets holding fewer than 10 KOs of the ranked universe. `MIN_SET_SIZE` is 5 because panel membership is still partial, below the usual GSEA floor of 10-15, so report size alongside any claim from a flagged set. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} write_csv(enrich |> select(-leadingEdge), "output-tables/07_fgsea_all_sets.csv") # leadingEdge is list-column (KO ids driving each set's ES); saved separately for lookups enrich |> select(pathway, source) |> mutate(leading_edge = map_chr(enrich$leadingEdge, \(x) paste(x, collapse = " | "))) |> write_csv("output-tables/07_fgsea_leading_edge.csv") ``` ::: # Carrier control A KO carried by one lineage moves with that lineage: if the lineage is a larger share at vents, the KO ranks toward the vent end whatever its function. This check removes that part. Each taxon's vent-vs-non-vent Cliff's delta is computed on the curated grain-4 taxon matrix exactly as for KOs; each KO's delta is regressed on the delta of its top carrier taxon (from 06), and fgsea is re-run on the residuals for the span sets. A span class that stays enriched after the control is vent-skewed beyond its carriers' turnover. >SKH: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} taxon_habitat <- build_matrix(paired_all, "cur_L4", min_tpm = 0, transform = params$transform, id_col = "sample_id", aggregate = "mean", unit_col = "sample_unit") taxon_delta <- tibble(top_carrier_L4 = colnames(taxon_habitat$z), delta_carrier = contrast_ranks(taxon_habitat$z, habitat_by_unit, focal = "Vent")) control_df <- ranks_df |> inner_join(taxon_delta, by = "top_carrier_L4") |> filter(is.finite(delta_carrier)) carrier_fit <- lm(delta_vent ~ delta_carrier, data = control_df) control_df$delta_resid <- residuals(carrier_fit) message(glue("KO delta ~ top-carrier delta: R2 = {round(summary(carrier_fit)$r.squared, 3)} ", "over {nrow(control_df)} KOs with a carrier")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` KO delta ~ top-carrier delta: R2 = 0.157 over 765 KOs with a carrier ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ranks_resid <- control_df |> arrange(desc(delta_resid)) |> select(ko_id, delta_resid) |> deframe() span_sets_resid <- map(span_sets, intersect, names(ranks_resid)) |> (\(x) x[lengths(x) >= MIN_SET_SIZE])() set.seed(params$seed) enrich_control <- fgsea(pathways = span_sets_resid, stats = ranks_resid, minSize = MIN_SET_SIZE, eps = 0) |> as_tibble() |> select(pathway, size, NES_resid = NES, padj_resid = padj) |> left_join(enrich |> select(pathway, NES, padj), by = "pathway") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning in prepareStats(stats, scoreType, gseaParam): There are ties in the preranked stats (32.55% of the list). The order of those tied genes will be arbitrary, which may produce unexpected results. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} enrich_control ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: > For results: span classes whose enrichment survives the carrier control. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} write_csv(enrich_control, "output-tables/07_fgsea_carrier_control.csv") ``` ::: # Sensitivity: order of tied ranks Cliff's delta between 13 vent and 6 non-vent units can only take values in steps of 1/78 (157 possible values), so many of the ranked KOs share a value and `fgsea()` warns that the order of tied KOs is arbitrary. Enrichment scores depend on that order. This check re-runs fgsea `N_TIE_DRAWS` times, each time adding jitter smaller than one third of the smallest gap between distinct values: the order **within** ties changes, the order **between** distinct values never does. The same check is applied to the carrier-control residuals. A set whose NES sign and BH call hold across draws does not depend on tie order. >SKH: assistant-added (2026-10-14). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} N_TIE_DRAWS <- 100 tie_draws <- function(stats, sets, n_draws = N_TIE_DRAWS) { gap <- min(diff(sort(unique(stats)))) if (!is.finite(gap)) gap <- 1e-6 purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(n_draws), \(i) { jittered <- stats + stats::runif(length(stats), -gap / 3, gap / 3) fgsea(pathways = sets, stats = jittered, minSize = MIN_SET_SIZE, eps = 0) |> as_tibble() |> # >SKH: same within-family BH as the main run (span-only residual runs are one family) mutate(family = unname(set_family[set_source[pathway]]) |> replace_na("span_rank")) |> mutate(padj = p.adjust(pval, method = "BH"), .by = family) |> select(pathway, NES, padj) |> mutate(draw = i) }) } summarise_ties <- function(draws) { draws |> summarise(NES_median = median(NES, na.rm = TRUE), NES_min = min(NES, na.rm = TRUE), NES_max = max(NES, na.rm = TRUE), padj_median = median(padj, na.rm = TRUE), padj_max = max(padj, na.rm = TRUE), frac_sig = mean(padj <= params$fdr_alpha, na.rm = TRUE), sign_stable = all(sign(NES) == sign(median(NES, na.rm = TRUE)), na.rm = TRUE), .by = pathway) } message(glue("Tied values: {round(100 * mean(duplicated(ranks) | duplicated(ranks, fromLast = TRUE)), 1)}% ", "of the main ranking, {round(100 * mean(duplicated(ranks_resid) | duplicated(ranks_resid, fromLast = TRUE)), 1)}% ", "of the carrier-control residuals")) set.seed(params$seed) tie_sensitivity <- bind_rows( tie_draws(ranks, all_sets) |> summarise_ties() |> left_join(enrich |> select(pathway, source, size, NES, padj), by = "pathway") |> mutate(ranking = "vent vs. non-vent delta", .before = 1), tie_draws(ranks_resid, span_sets_resid) |> summarise_ties() |> left_join(enrich_control |> select(pathway, size, NES = NES_resid, padj = padj_resid), by = "pathway") |> mutate(ranking = "carrier-control residual", source = "span_rank", .before = 1)) |> arrange(ranking, padj) tie_sensitivity |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
